reason: The cited evidence shows DSC can measure melting enthalpy and temperature in a specific HEA (E1), but provides no support for the claimed ±5% accuracy, high-throughput protocol, volume change measurement, or applicability to CoCrFeMnNi. E2 only defines configurational entropy and mentions DSC for heat capacity, not melting properties. Thus, most key premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: DSC/DTA can detect melting onset and enthalpy in HEAs with ±5% accuracy
High-throughput miniaturized crucibles and dual-atmosphere protocol are feasible up to 1600 °C
Volume change at melting can be deduced from simultaneous thermal analysis
Equiatomic HEAs like CoCrFeMnNi exhibit well-defined endothermic melting peaks
Conventional DSC baselines exist for comparison
